newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's Christmas Island casino to re-open.
newsitem.headline: Australia's Christmas Island casino to re-open.

text.p: The troubled Christmas Island casino will re-open on Friday with a new manager after a short closure, Christmas Island Resort (CIR) director Herman Gani said on Tuesday.
The casino, which had proved popular with high-rollers from neighbouring Indonesia, was closed in March after a dispute with its previous managers.
"We have commenced pre-opening activity to ensure that all systems and staff are at optimum performance before we return to full-scale operations," Gani said in a statement.
"We expect our international customers to resume visits to Christmas Island in the next few weeks." he said.

Former manager Casinos Austria International Ltd (CAIL) quit the casino on the island, an Australian Indian Ocean territory located 300 km south of Jakarta, after a protracted dispute with CIR, its Indonesian-controlled owner.

Australia's Territories Minister Warwick Smith said earlier this month that Casino Management International (CMI) Pty Ltd, a private company owned by businessman John Haddad, had been appointed to run the casino for 12 months until a new operator was named.
"We are looking forward to working with our new operator ... whose association with the Federal Hotels Group includes an excellent 25-year record managing casinos in Tasmania," Gani said.
CAIL said in March would claim substantial damages from CIR over what it said were breaches of its five-year casino management contract.
Gani said a court hearing between the two parties, set to resume in Perth on June 14, would have no bearing on the casino's re-opening.
